round_analysis.summary: Primary metric validation_accuracy and secondary metric epoch_time both moved favorably for most atomic primitives: 7 of 9 pipelines beat the baseline (0.6574 acc / 111.31s) on validation_accuracy, and 7 of 9 also beat baseline epoch_time. The best result was random_affine_translate (max_translate_fraction=0.1, p=0.5): acc 0.7308 (+0.0734/+11.2%) with epoch_time 104.57 (-6.74/-6.1%), a clean win. random_horizontal_flip (p=0.5) was a close second clean win (+0.0544 acc, -6.19 epoch_time). Photometric (color_jitter), occlusion (random_erasing) and mixing (mixup/cutmix) primitives split into wins, trade-offs, and one clear failure (mixup), while gaussian_noise was a mild negative. Two of the round's largest epoch_time movements look anomalous rather than mechanistic: weak color_jitter costs +26.8% time while the structurally similar but stronger moderate color_jitter costs -3.7%, a likely timing confound.

hypothesis_result.reason: Design fidelity is only partial: the exploration_objective named blur as a primitive family but no blur pipeline appears in the gradient; strategy_selection_rationale stated the occlusion primitive (random_erasing) would be duplicated across two strength levels for the round's diagnostic strength-sensitivity probe, but only one erasing config was run (area_ratio 0.02-0.2) — instead the strength duplicate that actually ran was on color_jitter (weak vs moderate), a different axis than planned; and the rationale explicitly excluded MixUp/CutMix ('per constraints') yet both were executed as pipelines 7 and 8. Given these deviations, the round did not fully test the hypothesis as designed. On the outcome that WAS produced: the core claim ('simple label-preserving batch perturbations can improve validation_accuracy without meaningfully increasing epoch_time, and the best basic direction can be identified') is supported for the geometric family — random_affine_translate and random_horizontal_flip both improved validation_accuracy (+0.0734 and +0.0544 vs baseline) while also lowering epoch_time (-6.05% and -5.56%), clean wins with no secondary-metric trade-off. But the 'without meaningfully increasing epoch_time' clause fails for random_erasing (+0.0268 acc but +9.3% epoch_time) and for weak color_jitter (+0.0042 acc but +26.8% epoch_time), and two primitives (gaussian_noise, mixup) regressed the primary metric outright. Net: direction-identification succeeded (geometric > photometric > occlusion > noise/mixup), but the joint accuracy+time claim only holds for a subset of primitives.

key_findings: Geometric primitives dominate the round on the primary metric with no secondary-metric cost: random_affine_translate (max_translate_fraction=0.1, p=0.5, batch) is the round's best result, acc 0.7308 (delta +0.0734/+11.2% vs baseline) with epoch_time 104.57 (delta -6.74/-6.05% vs baseline, better) — clean win. random_horizontal_flip (p=0.5, batch) is second, acc 0.7118 (+0.0544/+8.28%) with epoch_time 105.12 (-6.19/-5.56%, better) — clean win. Hypothesis: ImageNet-100 classes rarely depend on left-right orientation or small object position, so these cheap resample-only transforms add pose/position diversity without destroying class-discriminative content.

Controlled strength comparison on color_jitter (same op/scope, brightness/contrast/saturation/hue/p varied): weak (0.2/0.2/0.2/0.0/1.0) gives acc 0.6616 (+0.0042/+0.64%, small) with epoch_time 141.14 (+29.83/+26.8%, much worse); moderate (0.4/0.4/0.4/0.1/1.0) gives acc 0.6756 (+0.0182/+2.77%, larger) with epoch_time 107.15 (-4.16/-3.74%, better). Moderate wins on both metrics despite doing strictly more per-image computation than weak — this inversion is not mechanistically plausible for genuine op cost and is flagged as a timing confound rather than a real strength-vs-cost trend.

Mixing methods split sharply under an identical 'keep original hard label' design: cutmix (alpha=1.0, max_patch_area_ratio=0.25, p=0.5) is a clean win, acc 0.6956 (+0.0382/+5.81%) with epoch_time 101.40 (-9.91/-8.90%, better); mixup (alpha=0.2, p=0.5) is the round's worst primary regression, acc 0.6368 (-0.0206/-3.13%), though epoch_time also improved (-9.58/-8.61%) — a cost-saving failure, not a win. Hypothesis: CutMix's region replacement leaves most of the dominant object's texture/edges intact so the retained hard label stays valid, while MixUp's global pixel blend (even at low alpha=0.2) measurably corrupts the image-label correspondence for a same-strength probability of application (p=0.5 both).

random_erasing (area_ratio_range=[0.02,0.2], p=0.5) delivers a solid accuracy gain, acc 0.6842 (+0.0268/+4.08% vs baseline), but is paired with the round's second-largest epoch_time increase, 121.67s (+10.36/+9.3% vs baseline) — a trade-off. Unlike the jitter anomaly, this cost plausibly reflects real per-image mask generation/fill overhead rather than noise, since it is the only occlusion-type op and shows a consistent direction (accuracy up, cost up).

Combining flip+weak-jitter (pipeline 9, same weak-jitter params as pipeline 2) does not exceed flip alone as a controlled single-variable addition: acc 0.7102 (+0.0528/+8.03%) vs flip-alone's 0.7118 (+0.0544/+8.28%) — combo is slightly worse on the primary metric than the geometric primitive by itself, even though weak jitter alone was mildly positive (+0.0042). epoch_time for the combo (102.57, -7.85%) is better than flip-alone's (-5.56%), so there is no secondary-metric penalty for combining, but the primary-metric signal suggests weak jitter's isolated positive delta is not a real additive contributor once flip is present.

gaussian_noise (std=0.03, p=0.5) is a negative primary result, acc 0.6498 (-0.0076/-1.16% vs baseline), with epoch_time improving (-9.83/-8.83%) — a cost-saving failure, the mildest of the round's two negative-accuracy pipelines.
positive_signals: random_affine_translate (max_translate_fraction=0.1, rotate=0, scale=1.0, shear=0, p=0.5, batch): acc +0.0734/+11.2% vs baseline (best of round), epoch_time -6.74/-6.05% vs baseline (also better) — clean win; hypothesis: cheap translation-only shift adds spatial invariance without altering label-relevant content (mechanism, unverified).

random_horizontal_flip (p=0.5, batch): acc +0.0544/+8.28% vs baseline, epoch_time -6.19/-5.56% vs baseline (also better) — clean win; hypothesis: left-right mirror symmetry is a valid invariance for most ImageNet-100 object classes (mechanism, unverified).

cutmix (alpha=1.0, max_patch_area_ratio=0.25, p=0.5, keep_original_hard_labels, batch): acc +0.0382/+5.81% vs baseline, epoch_time -9.91/-8.90% vs baseline (also better) — clean win; hypothesis: capped patch area keeps the dominant object visible enough that the retained hard label stays valid while adding occlusion-style regularization (mechanism, unverified).
negative_signals: mixup (alpha=0.2, p=0.5, keep_original_hard_labels, batch): acc -0.0206/-3.13% vs baseline (worst of round), epoch_time -9.58/-8.61% vs baseline (better, but does not offset the accuracy loss) — cost-saving failure; hypothesis: global pixel blending breaks image-label correspondence even at low alpha when hard labels are kept unchanged (mechanism, unverified).

gaussian_noise (mean=0.0, std=0.03, p=0.5, clip=true, batch): acc -0.0076/-1.16% vs baseline, epoch_time -9.83/-8.83% vs baseline (better, but does not offset the accuracy loss) — cost-saving failure; hypothesis: even conservative additive noise at std=0.03 degrades fine-grained texture cues ResNet-50 relies on for closely related ImageNet-100 classes (mechanism, unverified).
tradeoffs: random_erasing (area_ratio_range=[0.02,0.2], aspect_ratio_range=[0.3,3.3], fill=mean, p=0.5, batch): acc +0.0268/+4.08% vs baseline (positive) but epoch_time +10.36/+9.3% vs baseline (worse) — accuracy gain comes with a real (non-noise-plausible) throughput cost.

color_jitter weak (brightness=0.2, contrast=0.2, saturation=0.2, hue=0.0, p=1.0, batch): acc +0.0042/+0.64% vs baseline (marginal positive) but epoch_time +29.83/+26.8% vs baseline (worst epoch_time regression of the round) — likely not a genuine op trade-off but flagged here since it is the only case where a primary gain paired with a secondary regression that large; treat with caution (see uncertainties).
uncertainties: No repeat-run or variance information is provided anywhere in the gradient; magnitude is the only heuristic available for significance. Small deltas (color_jitter weak +0.0042, gaussian_noise -0.0076) may fall within run-to-run noise.

color_jitter weak's epoch_time (+26.8% vs baseline) is inconsistent with color_jitter moderate's epoch_time (-3.74% vs baseline) despite moderate doing strictly more computation per image (larger ranges plus nonzero hue) — likely an infra/timing outlier (resource contention, cold start) rather than a real cost of the op; epoch_time deltas from single runs should not be trusted at face value for this op.

Batch-level augmentation volume/probability is not uniform across pipelines (p=0.5 for flip/noise/erasing/translate/mixup/cutmix vs p=1.0 for both color_jitter configs) and copies-per-sample / epoch count / batch size are not stated but presumably held constant — this is a confound when comparing absolute strength effects across ops, since p=1.0 jitter is applied to every image while p=0.5 ops only affect half the batch on average.

Design-plan deviations reduce confidence in cross-round comparability: no blur primitive was run despite being named in the exploration_objective; the planned weak-vs-moderate occlusion (random_erasing) strength probe was not executed (only one erasing config present); and mixup/cutmix were run despite the strategy_selection_rationale stating they were excluded — the actual round tested a different primitive set than the one the hypothesis text describes.
leads_from_this_round: Geometric ops (random_affine_translate, random_horizontal_flip) were the only clean wins with no secondary-metric cost (translate: +11.2% acc/-6.05% time; flip: +8.28% acc/-5.56% time) — this opens testing higher-strength or combined geometric configs (e.g., larger max_translate_fraction, or translate+flip together) while continuing to avoid photometric/occlusion additions that showed cost trade-offs.

The color_jitter weak-vs-moderate comparison showed moderate beating weak on both accuracy (+2.77% vs +0.64%) and epoch_time (-3.74% vs +26.8%), but the epoch_time relationship is mechanistically implausible and flagged as likely noise — re-running weak color_jitter (same brightness=0.2/contrast=0.2/saturation=0.2/hue=0.0/p=1.0) would clarify whether its epoch_time spike is real before drawing strength conclusions for the photometric family.

CutMix (region-based, +5.81% acc/-8.90% time, clean win) clearly outperformed MixUp (global blend, -3.13% acc/-8.61% time, cost-saving failure) under an identical hard-label-retention scheme — this opens exploring CutMix at different max_patch_area_ratio values rather than pursuing MixUp-style blending under the hard-label constraint.

random_erasing gave the largest occlusion-based accuracy gain (+4.08%) but at a real epoch_time cost (+9.3%), and the planned weak-vs-moderate occlusion strength duplicate never ran — a lighter erasing config (e.g., smaller area_ratio_range than [0.02,0.2]) is an open, untested comparison that could reveal whether a reduced-area erasing keeps most of the accuracy gain at lower time cost.

gaussian_noise (std=0.03) and mixup (alpha=0.2) were the only two primitives with negative primary-metric deltas, and both also had among the largest epoch_time reductions (-8.83%, -8.61%) — before ruling these families out, the parameter choice itself (noise std, mixup alpha, or the hard-label-retention scheme for mixup specifically) remains an open variable to probe.

round_analysis.summary: Primary metric validation_accuracy and secondary metric epoch_time were both measured against a single consistent baseline (acc 0.6574, epoch_time ~111.31s) across all 10 pipelines. Six of ten pipelines beat baseline accuracy, and two (random_affine_translate strong, and flip+translate stack) set new history-best accuracy (0.7434 and 0.7444) at near-baseline or better epoch_time, confirming geometric primitives remain the strongest, cheapest lever. The mixup-vs-cutmix alpha ablation cleanly isolated blend mechanism (not alpha) as mixup's failure cause. Occlusion methods (erasing-light, cutmix-small-patch, grid_mask) all improved accuracy but cost extra epoch_time (trade-offs, +2.6% to +9.3%). color_jitter pushed past 'moderate' both lost accuracy and produced a severe (+625%) epoch_time blowup, likely partly a measurement/implementation artifact. The stochastic 2-op composite underperformed the simple static flip+translate stack on both metrics.

hypothesis_result.reason: Design fidelity was good for most sub-tests: mixup's alpha was matched exactly to cutmix's (1.0), translate's strength/probability were both raised together, erasing's area and probability were both lowered together, and color_jitter's strength axis was extended by a further, consistent step. Outcomes were mixed: (b) mixup-vs-cutmix ablation is decisively resolved — mixup at alpha=1.0 still regressed accuracy (-0.0106 vs baseline) while cutmix at the same alpha improved it (+0.0454), so blend mechanism, not alpha, is confirmed as the driver, refuting the alpha-explanation sub-hypothesis. (d) color_jitter's ceiling is supported: strong setting reversed moderate's gain to -0.0104 accuracy and exploded epoch_time (+625.7%). (c) erasing's lighter config is only partially supported: accuracy gain survived and even grew (+0.0336 vs round-0's +0.0268) while the time penalty shrank from +9.3% to +2.56% but did not disappear. (a) geometric stacking is inconclusive: flip+translate stacked (11: +0.087 acc) barely beat translate-strength-alone (10: +0.086 acc), a 0.001 gap likely within noise, so additive stacking is not clearly demonstrated. (e) new families (blur, grid_mask, composite) added coverage but none exceeded the round's best pipelines on the primary metric.

key_findings: New history-best accuracy this round: random_horizontal_flip(p=0.5)+random_affine_translate(0.1,p=0.5) stack (pipeline 11) reached 0.7444 (+0.087 vs baseline, +13.23%) with epoch_time 110.25s (-1.06 vs baseline, better) — a clean win, but only +0.001 above translate-alone-at-higher-strength (pipeline 10: 0.7434), suggesting the two geometric effects overlap rather than cleanly add.

Controlled alpha-matched ablation isolates mixup's failure mechanism: mixup(alpha=1.0, global blend, hard labels retained) scored 0.6468 (-0.0106 vs baseline, worse) while cutmix(alpha=1.0, patch swap, hard labels retained) scored 0.7028 (+0.0454 vs baseline, better) — same alpha, opposite outcome, so blend mechanism (global pixel mix vs patch replacement) is the driver of round-0's mixup regression, not alpha choice.

color_jitter pushed to 'strong' (0.6/0.6/0.6/0.15, p=1.0) is the round's only clear failure on both metrics: accuracy -0.0104 vs baseline AND epoch_time 807.8s (+696.5s, +625.7% vs baseline) — an outlier far outside the 104-122s range of every other pipeline this round, consistent with round-0's already-flagged color_jitter timing instability.

Lowering random_erasing's area/probability (0.02-0.2,p0.5 → 0.02-0.08,p0.3) simultaneously improved accuracy (+0.0336 vs baseline, vs round-0's +0.0268) and shrank the time penalty (+2.56% vs round-0's +9.3%) — strength reduction helped both metrics relative to the heavier config, though time is still worse than baseline.

Shrinking cutmix's patch cap (0.25→0.15) improved accuracy further (+0.0454 vs baseline, vs round-0's +0.0382) but epoch_time worsened vs baseline (+4.08%) — accuracy trend supports the 'less occluded content preserves label validity' mechanism, but cost trend is unresolved without round-0's cutmix time for direct comparison.

The stochastic 2-op composite sampler (flip/translate/color_jitter/blur pool, 2 ops/batch) scored 0.723 (+0.0656 vs baseline) but underperformed the simple static flip+translate stack on both metrics (0.7444 acc / 110.25s vs composite's 0.723 acc / 112.27s), indicating automated per-batch diversification did not beat targeted hand-picked composition at these settings.

gaussian_noise repair (std0.03→0.01, p0.5→0.3) reversed round-0's negative sign to +0.007 vs baseline, and gaussian_blur (new family) landed at +0.008 vs baseline with a small time improvement (-2.72%) — both are directionally positive but small enough that significance is unknown without repeated-run variance data.
positive_signals: random_affine_translate(max_translate_fraction=0.15, probability=0.6, batch): acc 0.7434, +0.086 vs baseline (better), +0.0126 vs round-0's translate(0.1,p0.5) win — epoch_time 110.15s, -1.16 vs baseline (better). Mechanism (hypothesis): larger translation magnitude keeps improving spatial-invariance regularization without yet saturating.

random_horizontal_flip(p=0.5)+random_affine_translate(0.1,p=0.5) stack (batch): acc 0.7444, +0.087 vs baseline (better, new history best) — epoch_time 110.25s, -1.06 vs baseline (better). Mechanism (hypothesis): combining two cheap spatial regularizers stays net-positive though the marginal gain over translate-alone is small (+0.001), implying overlapping rather than fully additive benefit.

gaussian_blur(kernel=3, sigma=[0.1,1.0], p=0.3, batch): acc 0.6654, +0.008 vs baseline (better, small) — epoch_time 108.28s, -3.03 vs baseline (better). Mechanism (hypothesis): mild high-frequency softening adds gentle regularization without destroying texture cues the way additive pixel noise did; magnitude is small and significance unknown.
negative_signals: mixup(alpha=1.0, cross-sample, hard labels retained): acc 0.6468, -0.0106 vs baseline (worse) — epoch_time 109.03s, -2.28 vs baseline (better, cost-saving failure). Mechanism (hypothesis, confirmed by contrast with cutmix at same alpha): global pixel-space blending with retained hard labels creates a label-image mismatch that a patch-based swap avoids, so the mechanism itself — not alpha — is the failure cause.

color_jitter(brightness/contrast/saturation=0.6, hue=0.15, p=1.0, batch): acc 0.647, -0.0104 vs baseline (worse) AND epoch_time 807.80s, +696.49 vs baseline (drastically worse, +625.7%). Mechanism (hypothesis): strength beyond 'moderate' over-distorts color/texture cues needed for classification, and probability=1.0 at this strength appears to trigger a severe, likely non-linear compute cost (possibly an implementation/timing artifact given round-0's flagged color_jitter timing noise).
tradeoffs: random_erasing(area_ratio=[0.02,0.08], p=0.3, batch): acc 0.691, +0.0336 vs baseline (better) — epoch_time 114.15s, +2.84 vs baseline (worse, +2.56%). Reference: vs baseline.
cutmix(alpha=1.0, max_patch_area_ratio=0.15, cross-sample): acc 0.7028, +0.0454 vs baseline (better) — epoch_time 115.85s, +4.54 vs baseline (worse, +4.08%). Reference: vs baseline.

grid_mask(grid_ratio=0.3, spacing=[40,80], p=0.4, batch): acc 0.6878, +0.0304 vs baseline (better) — epoch_time 121.61s, +10.30 vs baseline (worse, +9.26%), a trade-off profile nearly identical to round-0's heavier random_erasing (+0.0268 acc/+9.3% time), so it does not clearly beat existing occlusion cost-efficiency. Reference: vs baseline.

random_op_sampler(pool={flip, translate, color_jitter_moderate, blur_mild}, 2 ops/batch, op_probability=0.5): acc 0.723, +0.0656 vs baseline (better) — epoch_time 112.27s, +0.96 vs baseline (worse, +0.86%), and underperforms the static flip+translate stack (pipeline 11) on both metrics simultaneously. Reference: vs baseline.
uncertainties: No repeated-run/variance data exists for any pipeline; small deltas (flip+translate vs translate-alone: +0.001; gaussian_noise repair: +0.007; gaussian_blur: +0.008) cannot be confirmed as real signal versus evaluation noise.

The per-metric 'last_round_best'/'history_best' references appear to come from different underlying pipelines for accuracy vs epoch_time (e.g., translate's epoch_time reads 'worse vs last round best' by +5.58s despite round-0 characterizing translate as having no epoch_time penalty), so cross-metric trade-off framing using that reference is likely confounded; vs-baseline (a single fixed reference of acc 0.6574 / epoch_time ~111.31s shared by all pipelines) is the more reliable basis used above.

color_jitter-strong's +625.7% epoch_time is a massive outlier inconsistent with every other pipeline's 104-122s range and echoes round-0's already-flagged color_jitter timing noise (weak vs moderate swing); it needs re-measurement before being trusted as a genuine compute cost rather than an implementation/timing artifact (e.g., a non-batched path triggered at probability=1.0).

Augmentation copies-per-sample and total training steps/epochs were held constant across every pipeline this round (single-pass batch-level augmentation), a shared confound that could mask whether stacking or stochastic composite benefits would emerge differently under longer training or multiple augmented views per sample.

cutmix-small-patch (+4.08% time) and grid_mask (+9.26% time) epoch_time increases vs baseline are directionally plausible for occlusion/patch compute cost, but without round-0's cutmix time value for direct before/after comparison, and without repeated-run variance, these cannot be confirmed as real costs versus scheduling noise.
leads_from_this_round: mixup(alpha=1.0) vs cutmix(alpha=1.0) controlled comparison confirms blend mechanism (global pixel mix vs patch swap) as mixup's failure cause, not alpha — opens either dropping the global-blend mixup family or testing a patch-restricted/local blend variant instead of pursuing further alpha tuning.

cutmix's smaller patch cap (0.25→0.15) improved accuracy further (+0.0454 vs +0.0382 baseline-relative) while epoch_time worsened +4.08% vs baseline — opens probing even smaller patch ratios (e.g. 0.05-0.10) to find the accuracy optimum while tracking whether time cost continues rising or plateaus.

random_erasing's area/probability reduction (0.02-0.2,p0.5 → 0.02-0.08,p0.3) simultaneously raised accuracy (+0.0336 vs +0.0268) and cut the time penalty (+9.3%→+2.56%) — opens testing further area/probability reduction to locate the point where time cost approaches baseline while accuracy gain is retained.

color_jitter's 'strong' setting reversed accuracy gain and produced a >6x epoch_time spike at probability=1.0 — opens re-measuring color_jitter's time cost in isolation across probability values (e.g. p=0.5 vs p=1.0) to separate a genuine strength-driven cost from a probability=1.0 implementation artifact before further exploring the strength axis.

Static flip+translate stack (0.7444 acc / 110.25s) beat the stochastic 2-op composite sampler (0.723 acc / 112.27s) on both metrics despite the composite's pool including those same two ops — opens testing a composite restricted to only the two proven geometric ops (dropping color_jitter/blur from the pool) or raising op_probability, to check whether pool dilution or op_probability=0.5 explains the underperformance.

Translate strength increase alone (0.1,p0.5→0.15,p0.6: +0.0126 relative) and flip+translate stacking (+0.0136 relative) produced nearly indistinguishable gains over round-0's translate win — opens testing translate strength beyond 0.15 in isolation (without flip) to check whether a ceiling exists independent of stacking effects.

round_analysis.summary: Primary metric validation_accuracy and secondary metric epoch_time were tested across 10 pipelines spanning geometric strength/axis probes, occlusion strength walks, a mixup scope repair, a composite-sampler ablation, and two new photometric families. The round's clear winner is random_op_sampler with pool=[flip,translate] and op_probability=0.8 (pipeline 25): new history-best on BOTH metrics (acc 0.745, +0.0006 vs prior best; epoch_time 106.6, -3.3% vs prior best), resolving round-1's composite underperformance. Elsewhere the round mostly produced diminishing-returns and reversal signals rather than new gains: translate pushed to 0.2 regressed accuracy (-0.0298 vs prior best), color_jitter's timing blowup persisted at halved probability (ruling out the p=1.0-artifact theory), cutmix's and erasing's strength-reduction trends both reversed/diminished below their round-1 sweet spots, and the mixup scope-repair recovered positive accuracy but at a steep +12.6% time cost. Photometric diversification split: sharpness was a clean modest win, PCA color augmentation was the round's only sub-baseline pipeline on accuracy.

hypothesis_result.reason: Design fidelity was good across all six hypothesis threads (each pipeline isolated the intended single variable: translate strength alone, translate+rotation vs translate+flip, identical color_jitter strength at halved probability, cutmix/erasing/grid_mask strength continuations, a patch-capped soft blend replacing global mixup, and two new single-mechanism photometric ops). Outcomes were mixed rather than uniformly confirming: (1) translate ceiling confirmed — pipeline 20 (0.2, p0.6) regressed acc to 0.7146, -0.0298 vs last-round-best; (2) rotation (pipeline 21) added no primary-metric gain over flip+translate (-0.0018, noise-level) but cut epoch_time -1.97% vs last-round-best, a cost win not an accuracy win; (3) the color_jitter probability-artifact theory was REFUTED — pipeline 22 at p=0.5 still shows +269% epoch_time vs baseline (vs +625% at p=1.0), meaning the cost is intrinsic to the strength config, not the probability; (4) the erasing/cutmix/grid_mask strength-reduction trend did NOT generalize cleanly — cutmix's accuracy delta fell from +0.0454 (0.15) to +0.0410 (0.08), erasing's further reduction (pipeline 24) shrank accuracy gain to +0.0172 with only marginal further time savings, and grid_mask's lighter config (pipeline 28) cut time cost sharply but also cut accuracy gain; (5) mixup's scope-repair (pipeline 26) turned a mechanism failure into a positive accuracy delta vs baseline (+0.0354), partially supporting the scope-vs-mechanism hypothesis, but reintroduced a +12.6% time cost; (6) diversification split, with random_sharpness succeeding cleanly and pca_color_augmentation underperforming baseline on accuracy.

key_findings: random_op_sampler(pool=[random_horizontal_flip, random_affine_translate], op_probability=0.8, scope=batch, pipeline 25) is the round's only clean win on both metrics: acc 0.745 (+0.0006 vs last-round-best, +0.0876 vs baseline) and epoch_time 106.596 (-3.32% vs last-round-best, -4.24% vs baseline), resolving round-1's composite underperformance likely by removing pool-dilution from color_jitter/blur and raising per-op application rate (hypothesis).

random_affine_translate(max_translate_fraction=0.2, probability=0.6, scope=batch, pipeline 20) regressed acc to 0.7146 (-0.0298, -4.0% vs last-round-best) while epoch_time stayed flat (-0.35 vs baseline, noise-level) — confirms a strength ceiling for isolated translate somewhere between 0.15 and 0.2, likely because larger shifts push label-relevant content out of frame (hypothesis).

color_jitter(brightness/contrast/saturation=0.6, hue=0.15, probability=0.5, pipeline 22) still shows +269% epoch_time vs baseline (410.85s vs 111.31s baseline) even at half the probability that produced +625% in round-1, while acc stayed flat (+0.01 vs baseline, -0.077 vs last-round-best) — this refutes the 'p=1.0 implementation artifact' theory and points to the strength config itself (large multi-channel perturbation) as the genuine bottleneck.

cutmix(max_patch_area_ratio=0.08, alpha=1.0, probability=0.5, cross-sample, pipeline 23) reversed the round-1 shrink-patch trend: acc delta fell from +0.0454 at 0.15 (round-1) to +0.0410 here, while epoch_time also failed to improve further (+0.158 vs last-round-best) — suggests the accuracy/cost optimum for cutmix's patch cap sits near 0.15, not below it.

random_erasing(area_ratio=[0.01,0.05], probability=0.2, scope=batch, pipeline 24) recovered a much smaller acc delta (+0.0172) than round-1's 0.02-0.08/p0.3 config while epoch_time only reached -1.1% vs baseline (essentially at baseline already) — the erasing strength-reduction trend has diminishing accuracy returns once pushed this far below round-1's setting.

grid_mask(grid_ratio=0.2, spacing=[60,100], probability=0.25, scope=batch, pipeline 28) cut the time penalty from round-1's +9.26% to near-zero (+0.42% vs baseline) but also shrank the acc gain from round-1's ~+4.6% relative to +3.3% relative here — the erasing-style 'lighter=better on both axes' pattern does not transfer cleanly to grid_mask, whose accuracy contribution appears more strength-dependent.

patch_soft_blend(max_patch_area_ratio=0.15, blend_alpha=[0.3,0.7], probability=0.5, cross-sample, pipeline 26) turned mixup's mechanism failure into a positive acc delta vs baseline (+0.0354) but at a +12.6% epoch_time cost vs baseline (125.38s) — the scope fix helps accuracy but the patch-restricted blend implementation itself is expensive, and it is dominated by cutmix which reaches similar/better accuracy near baseline-level time.

round_analysis.summary: Primary metric validation_accuracy and secondary metric epoch_time were both tracked against baseline (acc 0.6574, epoch_time ~111.31s) and history-best (acc 0.745, epoch_time ~106.60s, from round-2's 2-op sampler at op_probability 0.8). Every round-3 pipeline beat baseline on accuracy, but none beat history-best on accuracy; the closest was the 3-op geometric sampler (pipeline 33, 0.7406 acc, -0.59% vs history-best) which also nearly matched history-best epoch_time (106.63s, +0.03%). The round's diagnostic goals succeeded: color_jitter hue-only isolation showed no cost blowup (ruling out hue as the driver) and patch_soft_blend with fixed alpha eliminated its prior overhead entirely, becoming the round's fastest pipeline. But new-family exploration was costly: random_perspective produced the round's worst epoch_time regression (+112% vs baseline) for only mid-pack accuracy, and cutmix/grid_mask midpoints regressed on epoch_time as well as accuracy. Net effect: strong diagnostic progress, no net primary-metric advance past history-best, and one significant new secondary-metric liability introduced.

hypothesis_result.reason: Design fidelity was high across the round: each pipeline's parameters matched the stated diagnostic/refinement intent (translate at 0.17 between 0.15/0.2, sampler probability dropped to 0.6 with pool held fixed, color_jitter with only hue nonzero, patch_soft_blend with alpha fixed instead of randomized), so the three open questions from the hypothesis were genuinely tested rather than nominally touched. On outcome: the probability-ablation (pipeline 31) and hue-isolation (pipeline 34) diagnostics gave clear, attributable answers, and the patch_soft_blend repair (pipeline 40) fully resolved its cost question. However, the exploitation side of the hypothesis (push translate/sampler/rotation refinements past the 0.745 accuracy ceiling) failed everywhere in-round -- best result (pipeline 33, 0.7406) still trails history-best by -0.0044 (-0.59%) -- and one new family (random_perspective) introduced a severe, previously-unseen epoch_time regression (+112.3% vs baseline), so the round's stated goal of advancing the frontier while diversifying coverage was only partly achieved.

key_findings: random_op_sampler pool=[flip,translate,rotation(±15)], op_probability=0.6, ops_per_batch=2 (pipeline 33) is the round's standout: accuracy 0.7406 (+0.0832/+12.66% vs baseline, but -0.0044/-0.59% vs history-best 0.745) with epoch_time 106.628 (-4.68/-4.21% vs baseline, essentially tied with history-best 106.596, +0.03%) -- adding rotation to the proven 2-op geometric pool cost nothing on either metric while nearly closing the accuracy gap (mechanism hypothesis: a compatible, label-preserving geometric op adds diversity without new failure modes when the pool stays geometric-only, unlike round-1's mixed-family pool).

random_op_sampler probability-only ablation (pipeline 31: same [flip,translate] pool as history-best, op_probability 0.6 vs history-best's 0.8) shows accuracy fell to 0.7292 (-0.0158/-2.12% vs history-best) with only probability changed and pool held constant -- pins probability, not pool-narrowing alone, as a real driver of round-2's win. Epoch_time rose to 111.468 (+4.872/+4.57% vs history-best) despite the lower application rate, which is counterintuitive (fewer applications should not cost more) and likely reflects measurement noise rather than a real probability-cost relationship.

color_jitter hue-only isolation (pipeline 34: hue=0.15, brightness/contrast/saturation=0, prob=0.5) produced epoch_time 111.231, essentially flat vs baseline (-0.080/-0.07%) and nowhere near the historically-reported >250% blowup -- directly refutes hue as the sole cost driver (hypothesis: the blowup is a multi-channel/joint-computation artifact of combined brightness+contrast+saturation+hue processing, not hue-specific). Accuracy was also the weakest diagnostic result (0.6754, +0.018/+2.74% vs baseline but -0.0696/-9.34% vs history-best), suggesting hue alone carries little standalone accuracy value either.

This strongly supports that the prior cost blowup was randomization/sampling overhead, not the blend mechanism itself (hypothesis), though accuracy (0.6802, -0.0648/-8.70% vs history-best) remains uncompetitive on the primary metric.
