Design-fidelity gap: the round's hypothesis named 7 diagnostic threads but the gradient contains only 4 pipelines covering 2 of them (recombination, diversification); the sampler-ceiling/op_probability-lever claims, color_jitter multi-channel-cost claim, and patch_soft_blend/posterize repair claims from the pre-round hypothesis have no corresponding pipeline results and remain exactly as untested as after round 4.
positive_signals: random_solarize (threshold=0.5, probability=0.3, batch scope): accuracy 0.7004, delta_vs_baseline +0.0430 (+6.54%), epoch_time 99.77, delta_vs_baseline -11.54 (-10.37%) — clean win vs baseline reference (still -0.0446/-5.99% vs history_best). Mechanism hypothesis: threshold inversion preserves spatial/texture structure while adding a mild pixel-value perturbation, giving regularization without destroying class-discriminative texture.

random_grayscale (probability=0.2, batch scope): accuracy 0.6916, delta_vs_baseline +0.0342 (+5.20%), epoch_time 102.31, delta_vs_baseline -9.01 (-8.09%) — clean win vs baseline reference (still -0.0534/-7.17% vs history_best). Mechanism hypothesis: forcing reliance on shape/texture regularizes generically but removing all chrominance likely caps accuracy for color-dependent classes.

elastic_transform (alpha=15, sigma=4, probability=0.3, batch scope): epoch_time 102.48, delta_vs_baseline -8.83 (-7.93%) and delta_vs_history_best -4.11 (-3.86%), confirming the deliberately conservative strength avoided the severe resampling-cost blowup seen with random_perspective — a cost-side win, though its accuracy gain (+0.0188 vs baseline) was the smallest of the round's four pipelines.
negative_signals: cutmix stacked after the geometric sampler (pipeline 58: pool=[flip,translate] op_probability=0.8 + cutmix max_patch_area_ratio=0.15/alpha=1.0/probability=0.5, cross-sample scope): accuracy 0.7396, delta_vs_history_best -0.0054 (-0.72%), epoch_time 119.50, delta_vs_history_best +12.91 (+12.11%). Since s1 is identical to the history-best config, this isolates cutmix as the source of both the accuracy loss and the cost increase. Mechanism hypothesis: cutmix's patch coordinates are computed independent of the prior flip/translate, likely misaligning the mixed patch with the already-shifted image content and reducing label-region consistency, while adding its own per-batch blending compute.
tradeoffs: pipeline 58 (random_op_sampler[flip+translate, op_probability=0.8] + cutmix[patch=0.15, alpha=1.0, probability=0.5]) vs baseline: accuracy improves (+0.0822, better) while epoch_time worsens (+8.19 / +7.36%, worse) — a genuine trade-off at the baseline reference, even though the same pipeline is a clear failure (both metrics worse) at the history-best reference.
uncertainties: The planned history-best variance replicate was not run this round, so there is no same-condition noise estimate; the -0.0054 accuracy and +12.9% epoch_time gaps attributed to cutmix in pipeline 58 assume the s1-only history-best run is exactly reproducible, which is unverified.

Probability/strength was not held constant across the three new diversification families (grayscale probability=0.2, solarize probability=0.3, elastic_transform probability=0.3) — differences in their accuracy/cost could partly reflect this un-matched probability rather than a pure mechanism difference between the ops.

No repeated-run variance is reported for any epoch_time figure; given the round's own prior note that color_jitter's cost behavior was mechanistically surprising (pipeline 34 flat despite expectation), the cutmix +12.1% epoch_time delta and the diversification families' cost savings should be treated as unverified until a repeat-run check exists.

Five of the seven threads named in this round's hypothesis (probability knee/3-op pool, color_jitter channel isolation, patch_soft_blend/posterize strength recovery, cutmix repeat at 0.11, variance replicate) have no corresponding pipeline in this gradient, so the sampler-ceiling, op_probability-lever, and color_jitter-mechanism claims carried over from the pre-round hypothesis are neither confirmed nor refuted by this round's evidence.
leads_from_this_round: solarize (threshold=0.5, probability=0.3, batch) beat grayscale (probability=0.2, batch) on both accuracy (+0.88pp) and epoch_time (-2.54s) at the same scope; with solarize already 6.4% cheaper than history-best on epoch_time, there is cost headroom to test raising its threshold/probability to see if it can close more of the 4.46pp gap to the ceiling.

The controlled pipeline-58 comparison (identical s1 geometric sampler, cutmix added as s2) shows cutmix as a net-negative addition post-geometric (-0.72% accuracy, +12.1% epoch_time vs history-best) — this points to testing cutmix's cross-family interaction differently (e.g., applied before the geometric transform, or at lower probability/patch ratio) rather than sequential post-hoc stacking, since cutmix's standalone sweet spot (patch ratio 0.15) does not transfer cleanly into this composition.

elastic_transform (alpha=15, sigma=4, probability=0.3) proved cost-safe (-3.9% vs history-best epoch_time, no blowup) but delivered the weakest accuracy gain of the round (+1.88pp vs baseline, -6.88% vs history-best) — this opens whether raising alpha/sigma now that cost-safety is established at this conservative setting can recover more accuracy without reintroducing the random_perspective-style resampling cost.

Both grayscale and solarize landed well below history-best accuracy (-7.17% and -5.99% respectively) while being 4-10% cheaper than history-best epoch_time — no pipeline this round tested raising either family's probability/strength, leaving the round's own framing question ('can cheap families approach the ceiling at higher strength') unaddressed by evidence.

round_analysis.summary: Primary metric validation_accuracy and secondary metric epoch_time both stayed near baseline-plus levels but no pipeline exceeded the history-best accuracy of 0.745 (2-op geometric sampler, op_probability=0.8); the closest was pipeline 64 (2-op sampler, op_probability=0.7, acc=0.7404, epoch_time=106.33) which edged last_round_best (0.7396) by only +0.0008. The round's most consequential result is diagnostic, not exploitative: an exact replicate of the history-best config (pipeline 63) scored 0.7278 (epoch_time=111.16) instead of 0.745 (epoch_time=106.60), a same-condition swing of 1.72pp accuracy and 4.56s (4.3%) epoch_time, revealing a noise band large enough to make most of this round's (and prior rounds') small deltas non-attributable. Exploitation attempts (3-op pool at op_probability=0.8, patch_soft_blend area increase, elastic_transform strength increase) all failed to approach the ceiling and one (patch_soft_blend) reintroduced a real cost penalty (epoch_time +12.25 vs baseline, +16.96 vs history-best) while staying accuracy-weak.

hypothesis_result.reason: Design fidelity was good for all three stated goals: the probability×pool interaction was tested with a true single-variable change (op_probability 0.6->0.8 on the 3-op pool, pipeline 62), the noise estimate was obtained via an exact replicate of history-best (pipeline 63), and color_jitter's brightness channel was isolated at 'strong' magnitude (0.6) mirroring the prior hue-only test (pipeline 65). Outcome-wise the round did not close the gap to the ceiling: pipeline 62 (3-op@0.8) scored 0.7256, worse than both last_round_best (0.7396, -0.014) and history_best (0.745, -0.0194), showing the probability lever that helped the 2-op pool does not generalize to 3-op. The noise-estimate goal succeeded and is informative but negative for confidence: replicate pipeline 63 differed from the recorded history-best by -0.0172 accuracy and +4.56s epoch_time on an identical config, meaning several 'signals' claimed in earlier rounds (and even this round's own pipeline 64 edge over last_round_best of +0.0008) fall inside this noise band. The strengthening attempts on patch_soft_blend and elastic_transform (goal: raise accuracy floor without reintroducing cost) both failed on the primary metric and, for patch_soft_blend, also failed the cost-safety condition (epoch_time regressed 12.25s vs baseline).

key_findings: random_op_sampler (3-op pool: flip+translate+rotation, op_probability=0.8, batch scope, pipeline 62): acc=0.7256 (baseline +0.068 better, but last_round_best -0.014 and history_best -0.0194 worse), epoch_time=102.02 (baseline -9.29, history_best -4.58, both faster). Controlled comparison vs the round-3 3-op@0.6 config (acc 0.7406 per hypothesis text): raising probability from 0.6 to 0.8 on the SAME 3-op pool made accuracy worse by ~0.015, the opposite of the effect seen when raising probability on the 2-op pool (which produced the 0.745 ceiling) — the probability lever appears to interact with pool size/ops_per_batch rather than acting as a universal knob.

random_op_sampler (2-op pool: flip+translate, op_probability=0.8, exact replicate of history-best, pipeline 63): acc=0.7278 vs the recorded history-best value of 0.745 for the identical config (Δ=-0.0172), epoch_time=111.16 vs history-best's 106.60 (Δ=+4.56s, +4.3%). This is the first same-condition variance measurement obtained in the project and establishes a noise floor larger than most inter-pipeline deltas reported this round and in prior rounds.

random_op_sampler (2-op pool, op_probability=0.7, pipeline 64): acc=0.7404 (baseline +0.083, last_round_best +0.0008, history_best -0.0046), epoch_time=106.33 (baseline -4.98, history_best -0.264, both effectively cost-neutral vs history-best). This sits between the replicate's 0.7278 and the recorded 0.745, i.e. within the ~0.0172 noise band just measured, so it cannot be confidently called better or worse than op_probability=0.8 without repeated runs at both settings.

color_jitter (brightness=0.6 only, contrast/saturation/hue=0, probability=0.5, pipeline 65): acc=0.6616 (baseline +0.0042, essentially flat; last_round_best -0.078, history_best -0.0834), epoch_time=101.12 (baseline -10.19, history_best -5.48, both faster than history-best). Matches the earlier hue-only isolation's flat-cost/weak-accuracy profile, so brightness alone also fails to reproduce the previously observed color_jitter epoch_time blowup — with two of at least three channels now cleared, the blowup looks more like a joint multi-channel compute interaction than a single-channel effect (hypothesis).

patch_soft_blend (max_patch_area_ratio 0.15->0.25, fixed blend_alpha=0.5, cross-sample, pipeline 66): acc=0.6778 (baseline +0.0204 but last_round_best -0.0618, history_best -0.0672), epoch_time=123.56 (baseline +12.25 WORSE, last_round_best +4.05 worse, history_best +16.96 worse). Enlarging the blended patch area directly reintroduced the cost penalty the fixed-alpha version had previously eliminated, while accuracy stayed far below ceiling — suggests compute cost scales with patch area, and the accuracy shortfall is not simply an area-sizing problem.

elastic_transform (alpha 15->25, sigma 4->6, probability 0.3->0.4, pipeline 70): acc=0.6712 (baseline +0.0138, last_round_best -0.0684, history_best -0.0738), epoch_time=104.12 (baseline -7.19, history_best -2.48, faster). Strengthening warp magnitude did not move accuracy meaningfully above the family's previously reported 4.5-7pp-below-ceiling band (here 7.38pp below), while cost stayed controlled — the accuracy floor for this family looks warp-magnitude-independent within the range tested.

random_op_sampler+random_solarize recombination, sequential stack (pipeline 68, acc=0.7084, history_best -0.0366, epoch_time=101.15, history_best -5.45 faster) vs pooled integration (pipeline 69, acc=0.7202, history_best -0.0248, epoch_time=104.58, history_best -2.02 faster): holding the op set constant, folding solarize into the sampler pool beats sequential stacking on accuracy by +0.0118 at a +3.43s epoch_time cost — composition strategy matters, but neither form of solarize recombination reaches the pure geometric-only history-best (0.745), indicating any added op family currently dilutes rather than compounds the geometric sampler's benefit, though far less severely than the round-5 cutmix stack.
positive_signals: random_op_sampler (2-op: flip+translate, op_probability=0.7, batch, pipeline 64): acc=0.7404 vs baseline (+0.083, clean gain) and epoch_time=106.33 vs baseline (-4.98, faster) — cost-neutral-to-better relative to history-best epoch_time (-0.264). Mechanism hypothesis: intermediate probability may balance transform diversity against over-perturbation better than 0.8 for some runs. Caveat: the +0.0008 edge over last_round_best and the -0.0046 gap to history_best are both smaller than the 0.0172 noise band just measured on the identical-family replicate (pipeline 63), so this cannot yet be called a real improvement over the existing ceiling.
negative_signals: random_op_sampler (3-op pool: flip+translate+rotation, op_probability=0.8, pipeline 62): acc=0.7256, worse than last_round_best (-0.014) and history_best (-0.0194); epoch_time=102.02 improved vs both references. Reference: vs last_round_best and history_best. Mechanism hypothesis: at high per-op probability, adding a third op (rotation) to the pool likely over-perturbs batches, compounding rather than diversifying the geometric augmentation.

color_jitter (brightness=0.6, probability=0.5, batch, pipeline 65): acc=0.6616, worse than last_round_best (-0.078) and history_best (-0.0834); epoch_time=101.12 faster than both references. Reference: vs last_round_best/history_best. Mechanism hypothesis: strong brightness perturbation alone likely destroys enough low-level intensity cues for fine-grained ImageNet-100 classes to offset any regularization benefit.

patch_soft_blend (max_patch_area_ratio=0.25, blend_alpha=0.5 fixed, cross-sample, pipeline 66): acc=0.6778, worse than last_round_best (-0.0618) and history_best (-0.0672); epoch_time=123.56, worse than baseline (+12.25), last_round_best (+4.05) and history_best (+16.96) — a clear failure on both metrics. Reference: vs baseline/last_round_best/history_best. Mechanism hypothesis: larger patch area increases blend computation and likely introduces more label-inconsistent cross-sample content without enough of the primary image's discriminative region intact.

elastic_transform (alpha=25, sigma=6, probability=0.4, batch, pipeline 70): acc=0.6712, worse than last_round_best (-0.0684) and history_best (-0.0738); epoch_time=104.12 faster than both. Reference: vs last_round_best/history_best. Mechanism hypothesis: stronger elastic warp may introduce geometric distortions that no longer resemble natural pose/viewpoint variation, reducing its regularization value at ImageNet-100 scale.

random_autocontrast (probability=0.3, batch, pipeline 67, new family): acc=0.6854, worse than last_round_best (-0.0542) and history_best (-0.0596); epoch_time=110.31, worse than history_best (+3.71) though close to baseline (-1.0). Reference: vs last_round_best/history_best/baseline. Mechanism hypothesis: global per-channel contrast stretching is a mild, single-pass perturbation, likely too weak on its own to rival the geometric sampler's spatial diversity.
tradeoffs: random_op_sampler(2-op@0.8)+random_solarize sequential stack (threshold=0.5, probability=0.3, batch, pipeline 68) vs history-best pure geometric config: acc=0.7084 (history_best -0.0366, worse) while epoch_time=101.15 (history_best -5.45, faster) — cost-saving failure: cheaper but a real accuracy cost.

random_op_sampler with random_solarize folded into the pool (pool=[flip,translate,solarize], op_probability=0.8, ops_per_batch=2, batch, pipeline 69) vs history-best pure geometric config: acc=0.7202 (history_best -0.0248, worse) while epoch_time=104.58 (history_best -2.02, faster) — cost-saving failure, but milder than the sequential-stack variant (pipeline 68), showing pool-integration partially recovers accuracy at a smaller-but-nonzero cost saving.
uncertainties: The exact-replicate result (pipeline 63: acc=0.7278, epoch_time=111.16) vs the recorded history-best (acc=0.745, epoch_time=106.60) shows a run-to-run swing of 0.0172 accuracy and 4.56s epoch_time on an IDENTICAL configuration. Any delta in this round (or prior rounds) smaller than roughly this magnitude — including pipeline 64's +0.0008 over last_round_best and -0.0046 vs history_best, and pipeline 62's epoch_time gains of a few seconds — should be treated as within-noise, not a confirmed effect.

epoch_time itself shows unexplained variance even without any augmentation change (baseline-equivalent config swinging ~4.3% between pipeline 63 and the historical record for the same pipeline), so secondary-metric deltas under ~5s across this round's pipelines may reflect measurement/system noise rather than real per-op cost differences.

elastic_transform's strengthened config (pipeline 70, 7.38pp below ceiling) is compared only qualitatively to the hypothesis's stated 'round-5 4.5-7pp below ceiling' band since the exact round-5 elastic_transform value is not in this gradient — whether strengthening made it modestly worse or is within the same band cannot be confirmed from this data alone.

All pipelines in this round appear to hold augmentation volume/copies-per-sample and total training length constant (not varied by any pipeline) — if epoch count or schedule is fixed and short, small accuracy deltas across the many near-baseline pipelines (autocontrast, brightness-only jitter, elastic_transform) may be compressed by limited training exposure rather than reflecting each op's true asymptotic effect.
leads_from_this_round: The 2-op vs 3-op pool comparison at op_probability=0.8 (0.745-region vs 0.7256, pipeline 62) diverges from the 3-op pool's own probability=0.6 result (~0.7406), suggesting pool size and op_probability interact — worth mapping the 3-op pool at intermediate probabilities (between 0.6 and 0.8) rather than assuming the 2-op pool's optimal probability transfers directly.

The replicate's noise band (Δacc=0.0172, Δepoch_time=4.56s on an identical config, pipeline 63 vs recorded history-best) is now a concrete significance threshold; before trusting any probability-knee estimate (e.g. pipeline 64's 0.7404 at op_probability=0.7), repeated runs at the same setting are needed to separate a real knee from this measured noise.

color_jitter single-channel isolations (hue previously, brightness now at pipeline 65: acc 0.6616, epoch_time=101.12, both flat/fast) have cleared two channels without reproducing the family's known cost blowup — an isolation of the remaining channels (contrast, saturation) or a two-channel joint test would directly test whether the blowup is channel-specific or a joint-interaction artifact.

patch_soft_blend's area-ratio increase (0.15->0.25, pipeline 66) reintroduced cost (epoch_time +16.96 vs history_best) without recovering accuracy (-0.0672 vs history_best) — the area lever is not the fix; the mechanism (cross-sample patch blend with fixed alpha=0.5) itself, rather than patch size, looks like the accuracy bottleneck.

Pool-integrated solarize (pipeline 69: acc=0.7202, epoch_time=104.58) recovers more accuracy than sequential-stacked solarize (pipeline 68: acc=0.7084, epoch_time=101.15) at a modest +3.43s cost premium, holding the op set fixed — composition strategy (stack vs pool-member) is a lever distinct from op choice, and both remain below the pure geometric-only ceiling (0.745), so any further recombination attempt should track this stack-vs-pool axis explicitly rather than treating recombination as a single strategy.

round_analysis.summary: Primary metric validation_accuracy and secondary metric epoch_time both moved across 10 pipelines this round; baseline ≈0.6574 acc / 111.31s. The round's best pipeline (3-op geometric pool, random_op_sampler flip+translate+rotation @ p=0.7, p72) hit 0.7434 acc / 103.87s, essentially matching the 0.745/106.60s historical ceiling within a noise band that this round itself proved is wider than previously thought (~2.2pp / ~9.3s across three nominal replicates of the same 2-op config). Color_jitter's cost blowup was NOT reproduced by either remaining single channel (contrast p73, saturation p74), completing the 4-channel isolation and strengthening the joint-multi-channel hypothesis. Cutmix reordering (p75) and patch_soft_blend alpha isolation (p76) both failed to recover accuracy versus the geometric ceiling, with p76 additionally producing the round's worst epoch_time (+11% vs ceiling), an unexplained secondary-metric regression. New axes (scale/zoom p78, single-op-selection p79, channel permutation p80) gave a promising standalone geometric candidate, a fast-but-lower-accuracy composition alternative, and a weak/inconclusive photometric probe respectively.

hypothesis_result.reason: Design fidelity was high across all 10 pipelines: the diagnostic replicate (p71) exactly matched the recorded history-best op/params/scope, the color_jitter channel isolations (p73 contrast=0.6, p74 saturation=0.6) matched the intended 'strong magnitude, single channel' design, solarize (p77) was genuinely strengthened (threshold 0.4, prob 0.5) inside the specified pool-integration style, and the alpha-isolation (p76) changed only blend_alpha (0.5→0.3) holding area fixed as intended. Outcomes are mixed: the noise-band re-estimation objective succeeded and revealed an even wider band (~2.2pp/~9.3s across 3 measurements of nominally the same config) than round 6 estimated, meaning most of this round's small inter-pipeline deltas (p72, p77, p78 vs history/last-round best, all <0.02 acc) are not attributable. The color_jitter joint-channel hypothesis is now well supported (contrast and saturation both cleared the blowup, matching hue/brightness). The cutmix-order hypothesis is not supported: reordering did not recover accuracy vs the pure geometric config and added time. The patch_soft_blend alpha hypothesis was contradicted rather than confirmed: lowering alpha did not stay cost-safe, instead producing the round's worst epoch_time, an unexpected result with no clear mechanism yet.

key_findings: Diagnostic replicate random_op_sampler(flip+translate, op_probability=0.8, scope=batch) [p71] scored 0.7232 acc / 101.83s, extending the known noise band for this exact config to 0.745/106.60s (orig) → 0.7278/111.16s (round6 replicate) → 0.7232/101.83s (round7 replicate): a 2.18pp accuracy and 9.33s time spread, larger than the ~1.7pp/4.5s previously hypothesized, meaning virtually every other pipeline this round with a <0.02 acc delta vs last_round_best/history_best is statistically ambiguous.

color_jitter single-channel isolation completed: contrast-only (brightness=0,saturation=0,hue=0,contrast=0.6,prob=0.5) [p73] gave 0.6564 acc (-0.001 vs baseline, flat) / 101.20s (-10.11 vs baseline, fast); saturation-only (same structure, saturation=0.6) [p74] gave 0.694 acc (+0.0366 vs baseline) / 102.88s (-8.43 vs baseline, fast). Neither channel reproduces the family's prior cost blowup, and combined with previously-cleared hue/brightness, all four channels individually run fast — implicating a joint/combined-channel interaction as the blowup's source (hypothesis), not yet directly tested.

random_op_sampler(2-op flip+translate, p=0.8) plus solarize folded into the pool at matched probability (threshold=0.4, prob=0.5) [p77] scored 0.7388 acc / 102.93s vs the pure 2-op p71 at 0.7232 acc / 101.83s — a controlled, single-variable addition (solarize member) yielding +0.0156 acc for +1.10s (+1.1%), the round's cleanest attributable within-pool gain given it exceeds the noise floor established by p71's replicate history.

patch_soft_blend(area=0.15, blend_alpha=0.3, prob=0.5, cross-sample) [p76] produced 0.689 acc (still -0.056 vs history_best) alongside 118.29s epoch_time — the only pipeline this round slower than baseline (+6.98s) and the worst epoch_time of the round (+11.69s vs history_best, +11%), contradicting the isolation hypothesis that this variant would remain cost-safe like the prior 0.5/0.15 config.

random_affine_scale (zoom, scale_range=[0.85,1.15], prob=0.6, standalone) [p78] reached 0.7246 acc / 103.41s, nearly matching the full 2-op flip+translate combo (p71: 0.7232/101.83s) with a single op, at a modest +1.58s cost — suggesting scale carries comparable standalone invariance value to the existing pool members.

random_choice_single_op (uniform 1-of-5-op selection per batch) [p79] scored 0.7176 acc (below every other geometric/solarize pipeline this round) but 99.98s epoch_time, the fastest of the round (-6.61s vs history_best) — the guaranteed-single-op mechanism trades accuracy for the round's best efficiency, the opposite pattern from the probabilistic multi-op sampler pipelines.
positive_signals: random_op_sampler(pool=[flip,translate,rotation], op_probability=0.7, ops_per_batch=2) [p72]: acc 0.7434 (+0.086 vs baseline, better; +0.003 vs last_round_best, better but within noise band; -0.0016 vs history_best, worse but within noise) with epoch_time 103.87s (-7.44 vs baseline, -2.46 vs last_round_best, -2.72 vs history_best, all better) — matches-or-beats the ceiling at lower cost; mechanism hypothesis: intermediate probability better balances the previously observed 3-op pool's lower probability optimum vs the 2-op pool's 0.8 optimum.

random_op_sampler(pool=[flip,translate,solarize], op_probability=0.8, solarize_threshold=0.4) [p77] vs matched 2-op p71 (controlled: same base ops, same probability, solarize added): acc +0.0156 (0.7388 vs 0.7232) for epoch_time +1.10s (102.93 vs 101.83) — mechanism hypothesis: solarize's photometric perturbation is complementary to pure geometric invariance rather than redundant with it.

random_affine_scale(scale_range=[0.85,1.15], prob=0.6) [p78]: acc 0.7246 (+0.0672 vs baseline, better) roughly matching the 2-op combo's 0.7232 with a single op, epoch_time 103.41s (+1.58s vs p71) — mechanism hypothesis: scale/zoom invariance is a distinct, previously untapped geometric axis not covered by flip+translate+rotation.
negative_signals: patch_soft_blend(area=0.15, blend_alpha=0.3, prob=0.5, cross-sample) [p76]: acc 0.689 (-0.056 vs history_best, -0.0514 vs last_round_best, worse) and epoch_time 118.29s (+6.98 vs baseline, +11.69 vs history_best, worse) — mechanism hypothesis: blend interpolation compute or run noise, not the alpha reduction itself, likely drives the unexpected cost spike since lower alpha has no obvious reason to increase cost.

cutmix-then-geometric reorder [p75] vs pure geometric p71 (controlled: identical s2 sampler config, cutmix step added before it): acc 0.7218 vs 0.7232 (-0.0014, within noise) but epoch_time 104.03 vs 101.83 (+2.19s, +2.2% worse), and both accuracy references vs history_best/last_round_best are worse (-0.0232/-0.0186) — mechanism hypothesis: cross-sample patch mixing dilutes single-image class signal regardless of operation order, so reordering does not address the underlying dilution.

random_choice_single_op(5-op uniform pool, one op per batch) [p79]: acc 0.7176 (-0.0274 vs history_best, -0.0228 vs last_round_best, worse) despite epoch_time 99.98s (-6.61 vs history_best, best of round) — mechanism hypothesis: guaranteeing exactly one op per batch reduces per-sample augmentation diversity versus the 0-2-op probabilistic sampler, costing accuracy for speed.

random_channel_permutation(RGB shuffle pool, prob=0.2) [p80]: acc 0.6652 (+0.0078 vs baseline, likely within the ~0.022 noise band; -0.0798 vs history_best, worse) with epoch_time 101.51s (-5.08 vs history_best, better) — mechanism hypothesis: shuffling channel order removes color-based class cues relevant to some ImageNet-100 classes, offsetting any regularization benefit even at low probability.
tradeoffs: random_choice_single_op [p79]: primary metric worse vs ceiling (0.7176 vs 0.7434 best-of-round, -0.0258) while secondary epoch_time is best-of-round (99.98s vs 103.87s best-acc pipeline, -3.89s) — accuracy-for-speed trade-off versus the probabilistic multi-op sampler family.

random_op_sampler+solarize [p77]: primary metric gain vs matched 2-op baseline p71 (+0.0156 acc) paired with a secondary epoch_time increase (+1.10s, +1.1%) — small but real cost for the accuracy gain.

random_affine_scale [p78]: primary metric roughly flat vs p71 (+0.0014, within noise) while secondary epoch_time increases (+1.58s) — standalone op is not yet a clean win until paired with a real accuracy gain.
uncertainties: The noise band around the history-best 2-op geometric config is now measured at ~2.18pp accuracy / ~9.33s epoch_time across three nominal replicates (0.745/106.60s, 0.7278/111.16s, 0.7232/101.83s from p71) — nearly all of this round's deltas vs last_round_best/history_best (p72: +0.003/-0.0016; p77: -0.0016/-0.0062; p78: -0.0158/-0.0204) fall inside or near this band and should not be treated as ranked differences without repeat measurement.

patch_soft_blend's epoch_time spike (118.29s, p76) is a single measurement with no repeated-run variance data; given lowering blend_alpha has no obvious cost mechanism, this could be system/timing noise rather than a genuine property of alpha=0.3 — needs its own replicate before drawing conclusions.

Color_jitter's joint-multi-channel blowup hypothesis is inferred from four single-channel clears (hue, brightness, contrast p73, saturation p74) but no pipeline this round directly tested a 2+-channel joint combination, so the mechanism remains unconfirmed.

Augmentation volume/copies-per-sample and total training steps appear held constant across all 10 pipelines this round (never varied) — a uniform confounder that could itself be limiting the accuracy ceiling independent of op composition, and none of this round's evidence speaks to it.
leads_from_this_round: p72 (3-op pool, op_probability=0.7) is the round's top accuracy result (0.7434) but its edge over history_best (-0.0016) and last_round_best (+0.003) is inside the newly-measured ~2.2pp noise band — a repeat measurement of this exact config would clarify whether 0.7 is a real probability optimum for the 3-op pool before further probability sweeps.

All four color_jitter channels (hue, brightness, contrast p73, saturation p74) individually stayed fast (epoch_time 101-103s, no blowup), which opens testing a 2-channel joint combination (e.g., contrast+saturation together) to check whether the blowup requires ≥2 simultaneous channels.

Solarize folded into the 2-op pool at matched probability (p77 vs p71: +0.0156 acc for +1.1s) is the cleanest attributable within-pool gain this round — isolating solarize's own probability/threshold further within this same pool-integration style (rather than sequential stacking) is the opening this comparison supports.

random_affine_scale standalone (p78) nearly matched the full flip+translate combo (0.7246 vs 0.7232) for +1.58s — this opens testing scale as an additional pool member (analogous to how solarize was added) rather than only as a standalone op.

cutmix reordering (p75) did not close the gap to the geometric ceiling on either accuracy (-0.0014 vs p71) or cost (+2.19s vs p71), closing off operation-order as the explanation for cutmix's stacking penalty — the evidence points toward other variables (patch area, probability) as the next thing to isolate for cutmix rather than order.

patch_soft_blend's blend_alpha=0.3 config (p76) produced the round's worst epoch_time (118.29s, +11% vs ceiling) with no clear mechanism — this opens a need for a same-config replicate to check if the cost spike is real before attributing it to blend_alpha as a variable.

random_channel_permutation at prob=0.2 (p80) gave only +0.0078 acc vs baseline, inside the measured noise band, and clearly trailed the ceiling (-0.0798 vs history_best) — inconclusive at this probability; a higher-probability or repeated test is the concrete next step this evidence opens before ruling the op in or out.

round_analysis.summary: Primary metric validation_accuracy and secondary metric epoch_time both moved across the round's 9 pipelines, but the round's central diagnostic (p81, an exact replicate of round-7's top 3-op geometric pool) showed accuracy diverging by 0.0252 (0.7182 vs round-7's 0.7434) for an IDENTICAL config while epoch_time diverged by only 0.43s — confirming the accuracy noise band is real and even larger than the ~2.2pp previously estimated, while undercutting the ~9.3s epoch_time noise estimate. Given that, most of this round's near-ceiling accuracy results (p82 scale-in-pool 0.7398, p83 solarize-in-pool@0.7 0.7232, p87 cutmix-in-pool 0.7402) sit within or near that noise band relative to round-7's 0.7434 and history-best 0.745, so none can be confidently declared a new optimum. The clearer, more attributable results this round are on epoch_time: histogram_equalize (p89) produced a severe +31.99s (+28.7%) cost blowup versus baseline for only +0.0278 accuracy, and patch_soft_blend@alpha=0.3 (p86) reproduced a consistent ~+7-9s cost penalty across two independent rounds (118.29s round-7, 120.47s round-8) alongside consistently sub-ceiling accuracy (0.689, 0.674), confirming that spike is a real property of the op rather than measurement noise. The joint-channel color_jitter diagnostic (p85, contrast+saturation together) did not reproduce the historical cost blowup at all (100.32s, faster than baseline), leaving the joint-interaction cost hypothesis unconfirmed.

hypothesis_result.reason: Design fidelity was generally good: pipelines correctly instantiated the intended pool-integration recombination (p82 scale-in-pool, p87 cutmix-in-pool, p83 solarize-in-pool@0.7, p84 4-op combined pool), the ops_per_batch/op_probability ablation (p88), the joint-channel color_jitter probe (p85), and exact replicates for the noise-band check (p81) and patch_soft_blend cost spike (p86). Outcome is mixed: the noise-band premise was confirmed but recalibrated upward for accuracy (0.0252 divergence on an identical config, vs the stated ~0.022) and downward for epoch_time (0.43s divergence vs the stated ~9.3s), which undermines confidence in every 'improvement' this round smaller than ~2.5pp accuracy — including the extended pool-integration wins for scale (p82, +0.0824 vs baseline but only -0.0036 vs last-round-best) and cutmix (p87, +0.0828 vs baseline but only -0.0032 vs last-round-best), both of which are statistically indistinguishable from round-7's ceiling rather than clear new gains. The patch_soft_blend repair-check (p86) succeeded unambiguously (cost spike confirmed real via consistent direction across two rounds). The color_jitter joint-channel cost hypothesis was directly tested but NOT confirmed (epoch_time stayed fast, 100.32s). The ops_per_batch/op_probability disentanglement (p88) was inconclusive because its effect size (-0.0078 acc) is smaller than the round's own measured noise floor (0.0252).

key_findings: Exact replicate p81 (random_op_sampler, pool={flip,translate,rotation}, op_probability=0.7, ops_per_batch=2, scope=batch) of round-7's top config produced acc=0.7182 vs round-7's 0.7434 for the identical config (-0.0252, i.e. -3.4%) while epoch_time only diverged by +0.43s (104.30 vs 103.87) — accuracy noise is confirmed larger than the ~2.2pp prior estimate, epoch_time noise is smaller than the ~9.3s prior estimate; the two metrics do not share the same noise magnitude.

Controlled op-swap within the pool-integration pattern (rotation->scale, same pool skeleton {flip,translate,X}, same op_probability=0.7, ops_per_batch=2): p82 (scale) reached acc=0.7398/epoch_time=101.50s vs p81 (rotation) acc=0.7182/epoch_time=104.30s — scale is both faster (-2.8s) and nominally higher-accuracy, though the accuracy gap is within the round's own noise band so the ranking is not confidently established (hypothesis: scale/zoom is a cheaper affine op than rotation while providing comparable label-preserving diversity).

Cutmix-as-pool-member (p87, random_op_sampler pool={flip,translate,cutmix(patch_ratio=0.10)}, prob=0.8) reached acc=0.7402 (+0.0828 vs baseline, only -0.0032 vs last-round-best) after every prior sequential-stacking attempt (rounds 5, 7) failed — design matches the intended composition-style repair, and the result is directionally consistent with solarize's earlier pool-integration rescue, but given the p81 noise finding this single data point cannot yet be separated from noise at the top of the range.

Combining the two independently-positive adds into one 4-op pool (p84: {flip,translate,scale,solarize}, op_probability lowered to 0.6, ops_per_batch=2) produced acc=0.7038, clearly below both single-add variants (p82 0.7398, p87 0.7402/p83's solarize alone 0.7232) by margins (-0.036, -0.036, -0.019) that exceed this round's own noise floor (0.0252) — this is a real dilution effect, not compounding, even though epoch_time kept improving (100.31s, fastest pool config of the round).

patch_soft_blend@alpha=0.3 (cross-sample scope) reproduced a real epoch_time penalty across two independent rounds: round-7 118.29s (+6.98s/+6.3% vs this round's baseline reference) and round-8 replicate 120.47s (+9.16s/+8.2% vs baseline) — consistent sign and similar magnitude across replicates indicates the cost spike is a genuine property of the op, not measurement artifact, while accuracy stayed well below the geometric-pool cluster in both runs (0.689, 0.674 vs ~0.71-0.74 for pool configs).

color_jitter joint 2-channel test (contrast=0.6, saturation=0.6 simultaneously, batch scope) ran fast (epoch_time=100.32s, -10.99s vs baseline) rather than reproducing the historical blowup, directly weakening the joint-channel-interaction cost hypothesis; accuracy was also only marginally above baseline (0.6642, +0.0068), so the diagnostic clarified cost but left the op's accuracy value unresolved.

New diversification op random_equalize (prob=0.3, previously assumed cost-neutral like solarize/sharpness/posterize) produced the round's worst epoch_time by a wide margin: 143.30s, +31.99s (+28.7%) vs baseline and +36.7s vs history-best, for only +0.0278 accuracy vs baseline — contradicts the stated expectation that conservative-probability photometric ops are cost-neutral, implying the cost driver here is intrinsic to the op's implementation rather than its probability/strength.
positive_signals: random_op_sampler pool={flip,translate,scale(0.85-1.15)}, op_probability=0.7, ops_per_batch=2, batch scope (p82): acc +0.0824 vs baseline (0.7398), epoch_time -9.81s vs baseline and -2.37s vs last-round-best (101.50s) — faster than the rotation-based equivalent (p81, 104.30s) at comparable accuracy; reference vs baseline for accuracy, vs last-round-best for epoch_time; mechanism hypothesis: scale/zoom is computationally cheaper than rotation while offering similar label-preserving affine diversity.

random_op_sampler pool={flip,translate,cutmix(patch_ratio=0.10,alpha=1.0)}, op_probability=0.8, ops_per_batch=2, batch scope (p87): acc +0.0828 vs baseline (0.7402, the round's single highest raw accuracy), epoch_time -7.02s vs baseline; reference vs baseline; mechanism hypothesis: pool-membership (probabilistic per-op sampling) avoids the misalignment/dilution that hurt cutmix under sequential pre/post stacking in rounds 5 and 7.
negative_signals: random_equalize(probability=0.3), batch scope (p89): epoch_time +31.99s vs baseline (+28.7%, worst of the round and of project history per delta_vs_history_best +36.7s), for only +0.0278 accuracy vs baseline; reference vs baseline and vs history-best; mechanism hypothesis: per-channel histogram equalization has a much heavier per-image compute cost than the other 'cheap' photometric ops it was assumed to resemble.

patch_soft_blend(max_patch_area_ratio=0.15, blend_alpha=0.3, probability=0.5), cross-sample scope (p86): epoch_time +9.16s vs baseline (worse), acc 0.6742 sits -0.0692 below last-round-best and -0.0708 below history-best despite being +0.0168 above baseline; reference vs baseline for cost, vs last-round-best/history-best for accuracy shortfall; mechanism hypothesis (now supported by replication): cross-sample patch sourcing plus alpha-blending carries a genuine per-batch compute/memory overhead, and label-preserving-but-visually-ambiguous blended patches likely dilute the learning signal versus geometric-only augmentation.

random_op_sampler pool={flip,translate,scale,solarize}, op_probability=0.6, ops_per_batch=2, batch scope (p84): acc 0.7038 is -0.0396 below last-round-best and -0.036/-0.036 below the two single-add variants it combines (p82, p87), exceeding the round's own noise floor; reference vs last-round-best and vs sibling pipelines; mechanism hypothesis: adding a 4th pool member while holding ops_per_batch at 2 lowers each op's effective per-batch inclusion rate, diluting the signal from either add rather than compounding their gains.
tradeoffs: random_equalize(probability=0.3), batch scope (p89): accuracy improves marginally vs baseline (+0.0278) but epoch_time worsens severely vs baseline (+31.99s/+28.7%) and vs history-best (+36.7s/+34.4%); reference vs baseline — a modest primary gain is dominated by a large secondary cost regression.

random_op_sampler 4-op pool {flip,translate,scale,solarize} @ prob 0.6, batch scope (p84): epoch_time improves the most of any pool variant this round (-10.99s vs baseline, fastest pool config) but accuracy is the weakest of the pool-integration family tested this round (0.7038, -0.036 vs its two single-add siblings); reference vs baseline for cost, vs sibling pipelines for accuracy — cost savings come at a disproportionate accuracy cost relative to the simpler recombinations.
uncertainties: The p81 replicate shows accuracy noise (0.0252) exceeding the previously-cited ~2.2pp band, while epoch_time noise (0.43s) is far below the previously-cited ~9.3s band for the same identical config — the two noise estimates are inconsistent with each other and with prior rounds, so it is unclear which epoch_time deltas in this round (many pool variants differ by only 1-3s) are real vs noise; only the very large cost movements (p89 +31.99s, p86 +9.16s, p84/p85 -10.99s) look safely outside plausible noise.

Given the confirmed ~2.5pp accuracy noise floor, the round's near-ceiling results (p82 0.7398, p83 0.7232, p87 0.7402, p81 0.7182) cannot be confidently ranked against each other or against round-7's 0.7434/history-best 0.745 — the 'pool-integration extends to scale and cutmix' pattern is suggestive but not statistically separable from the noise just measured in this same round.

Augmentation volume/copies-per-sample and training schedule (epochs/steps) appear held constant across all 9 pipelines this round — only pool composition, membership style, and op_probability varied — so a fixed short training schedule could itself be an uncommon amplifier of the observed run-to-run accuracy noise; this was not tested and remains a standing confound across the whole exploration.

color_jitter joint-channel result (p85, acc 0.6642, +0.0068 vs baseline) is close enough to baseline that it may not reflect any real accuracy effect of the op at all; the diagnostic resolved the cost question (no blowup at 2 channels) but leaves the accuracy value of color_jitter unresolved and untested at 3+ simultaneous channels.

patch_soft_blend's cost-spike magnitude differs between the two replicates by 2.18s (118.29s vs 120.47s) — similar order to the general epoch_time noise uncertainty above — so while the direction (real cost penalty) looks robust, the exact magnitude of the true penalty is not well pinned down.
leads_from_this_round: cutmix-in-pool (random_op_sampler, pool={flip,translate,cutmix(patch_ratio=0.10)}, prob=0.8) reached the round's top raw accuracy (0.7402) after repeated stacking failures, but the single result sits within the round's confirmed ~2.5pp noise band relative to round-7's ceiling — a replication of this exact cutmix-in-pool config (mirroring the p81 approach) would separate a genuine composition-style fix from noise before further cutmix tuning.

scale-in-pool (random_op_sampler, pool={flip,translate,scale(0.85-1.15)}, prob=0.7) was both accuracy-competitive (0.7398) and the fastest of the top-cluster configs (101.50s vs 104.30s for the rotation-based equivalent) — a direct scale-vs-rotation-vs-cutmix comparison as the third pool member at matched probability/replicate count would clarify whether scale's epoch_time edge is a real, reusable cost saving.

4-op combined pool (scale+solarize, prob=0.6) underperformed both single-add variants by margins exceeding the noise floor while gaining epoch_time — suggests either raising ops_per_batch when pool size grows (to preserve effective per-image augmentation rate) or restricting combined-add experiments to one geometric + one photometric op at a time, rather than stacking two previously-independent winners at reduced probability.

color_jitter's historical epoch_time blowup was not reproduced by the 2-channel (contrast+saturation) joint test (100.32s, faster than baseline) — the cost-mechanism probe should be extended to other channel pairs (e.g. hue+saturation) or 3+ simultaneous channels before concluding the blowup is unrelated to channel count.

patch_soft_blend(alpha=0.3)'s cost penalty (+7-9s vs baseline) and sub-ceiling accuracy (0.674-0.689) replicated consistently across two independent rounds — this op family now has two converging negative data points rather than one ambiguous one, which is different evidence quality than a fresh negative result and should be weighed accordingly.

random_equalize(prob=0.3) produced by far the worst epoch_time of the round (143.30s, +28.7% vs baseline) despite conservative probability tuning modeled on the safe solarize/sharpness/posterize family — an isolated cost-only diagnostic (varying only probability/strength, no accuracy claim) would clarify whether the op's overhead is fixed-per-application (and thus reducible via lower probability) or fixed-per-batch regardless of strength.

The ops_per_batch=1 ablation (p88, same pool/probability=0.7 as p81) produced a difference (-0.0078 acc, -1.2s epoch_time) smaller than this round's own measured noise floor (0.0252 acc) — disentangling ops_per_batch from op_probability will need either a replicated ablation or a larger parameter step to produce a signal exceeding the newly-characterized noise band.
